title: Problem awareness — inside a GLP-1 gut

beats.text: This is what's happening inside your gut. A GLP-1 causes your appetite to slow down, and suddenly going to the bathroom gets harder.
beats.visual: Translucent character stops mid-bite with a sharp expression of discomfort as the interior stomach becomes visible; movement already underway in frame one. No swelling into obstruction.
beats.why: Preserve the user's exact hook. The appetite/bathroom contradiction creates immediate recognition while the anatomical view promises an explanation.

beats.text: Watch the stomach. Food moves through it with muscular contractions. A GLP-1 can slow how quickly that food leaves. See how it stays there longer instead of passing through at the same pace?
beats.visual: Side-on illustrative stomach follows food through continued contractions and a slower exit. Hold one legible action; label illustration. No precise retention time shown.
beats.why: Uses deictic language to direct attention to a changing process rather than merely naming an organ. Does not imply full gastric paralysis.

beats.text: You feel full for longer. And when constipation becomes part of the picture, you want digestion to feel comfortable again. Before choosing a supplement, follow what its ingredients actually do.
beats.visual: New dining-room wide view: character sets plate aside, shifts uncomfortably and looks toward an interrupted daily activity. No promised post-product result.
beats.why: Turns the mechanism into an everyday cost and a specific desire before introducing a solution. Constipation is not declared to have one universal cause.

beats.text: First, there's a plant compound in celery called apigenin. In mice fed a high-fat diet, it reduced inflammatory signals in the colon and helped normalize certain muscle responses. That research doesn't show that celery makes a GLP-1 stomach empty faster.
beats.visual: Celery macro, then a clearly labeled MOUSE STUDY research diagram of the colon. Indicate lower inflammatory markers and studied contraction responses, not restored human stomach emptying. No brand or product.
beats.why: Explains a concrete observed action and its experimental context. A mouse-colon illustration cannot masquerade as the viewer's proven product response.

beats.text: Second, chlorophyllin, a derivative of the green pigment in plants. It's been studied for odor control, with mixed findings. Reducing odor isn't the same thing as removing gas or relieving constipation.
beats.visual: Distinct chlorophyllin ingredient dish, followed by separate ODOR and GAS VOLUME labels. No bubbles disappear and no bloating before/after is shown.
beats.why: Separates the endpoint investigated from the desired digestive symptom; avoids assigning an unestablished action to chlorophyllin.

beats.text: Third, prebiotic fiber. Watch a type called FOS reach the large intestine, where beneficial bacteria use it as food. That fermentation can also produce gas, so tolerance matters.
beats.visual: FOS reaches a distinct colon microenvironment and is used by resident microbes. A small gas bubble appears without pathological pressure symbolism.
beats.why: Shows the supported prebiotic action at its actual location and includes the relevant tolerance limitation.

beats.text: These ingredients can be combined in a supplement. That doesn't establish that the combination treats GLP-1 constipation.
beats.visual: Three neutral ingredient labels group together. No arrows imply a proven shared treatment outcome. Hold the qualification at readable size with narration.
beats.why: All ingredient explanation is complete before brand entry; the synthesis distinguishes a combined formula from a proven combined treatment mechanism.

beats.text: Motilli brings celery, chlorophyllin and prebiotic fiber together in two daily gummies, without separate ingredients to measure or mix.
beats.visual: First Motilli pack and logo reveal on 'Motilli'; two accurate gummies and ingredient callouts. No earlier branding.
beats.why: Makes the product format concrete after explaining each ingredient. Does not claim the gummy reproduces a study's dose or efficacy.

beats.text: Take them as directed with water. If you're looking for these ingredients in one daily supplement, tap to shop Motilli, backed by a 90-day money-back guarantee.
beats.visual: Character's evening water-and-gummy routine, then product and Shop Motilli with verified guarantee. New composition; no symptomatic transformation.
beats.why: Closes on the actual offered formula and seller-listed policy. Treatment superiority or bodily outcomes are not invented to close the sale.

beats.visual: Hold package and readable CTA, music resolves.
beats.why: Three seconds to read and act; not extra efficacy messaging.

status: Full factual alternative, no placeholders. Does not claim a substantiated three-ingredient GLP-1 constipation UMS.

title: Solution awareness — MiraLAX and fiber

beats.text: This is what happens when you take MiraLAX or bulking fiber for constipation on a GLP-1. Watch where each one works.
beats.visual: Split view with PEG-associated stool hydration on one side and psyllium gel hydration on the other; both actions begin immediately.
beats.why: Directly pays off the comparison promise with distinct visible processes. Neither side is depicted as inevitably failing.

beats.text: Here, MiraLAX holds water in your stool, helping it soften and pass. Over here, a bulking fiber like psyllium absorbs water and helps form stool. Both can help you go.
beats.visual: Remain in split demonstration; highlight PEG on 'Here' then psyllium on 'Over here'. Continuous narration; no unnecessary base-shot cut.
beats.why: The language guides the viewer through a real distinction and preserves the treatments' supported usefulness.

beats.text: Now look higher up. A GLP-1 can slow food leaving the stomach. Softening stool doesn't necessarily change that. If you're still uncomfortable, you want to understand the difference before choosing another product.
beats.visual: Spatial move to a separate stomach view, then distinct character shot after a small meal. No implication that colon and stomach are one plug of waste.
beats.why: Builds the canonical spatial contrast without asserting that constipation remedies are useless. Unresolved discomfort creates a reason for the subsequent explanation.
